newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia rubber prices soften in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia rubber prices soften in late trading.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 offer prices softened in late trading on Monday but traders said possible near-term tight supply might limit the downside.
"Offer prices have softened a bit because of the absence of buyers. I believe buyers have also sidelined because they want to see a further decline in prices," one trader said.

Traders said offer prices were quoted at 53.25-50 U.S. cents/lb fob Palembang. In Medan, levels were quoted at 53.50, down 0.25 cents. In Surabaya SIR20 was offered at 53.25, down from 53.625 last week while in Padang, offer prices fell to 53.00 from 53.625 U.S. cents/lb last week.
In Pontianak and Jambi, traders offered SIR20 at 53.00, down from 53.25.50 last week, and traders also heard deals were done at 53.25 in Palembang on Friday night.
"We don't hear any fresh deals done in the market today. Prices are soft because of sluggish demand," said one trader.
But some traders believed tight supply and the current wintering would help limit offer prices to decline further.

Regional traders said the Southeast Asian rubber market was expected to wallow in the doldrums this week due to sluggish demand, and that curbs on supply from the current wintering were unlikely to support prices.
